questions.q: A point charge is placed in a moving train. A passenger A sitting in the train and person B on the ground observe the fields due to this charge. Then
options: A observes both electric and magnetic fields
B observes both electric and magnetic fields
questions.explanation: The charge is at rest relative to passenger A, so A observes only an electric field. The charge moves relative to B on the ground, so B observes both electric and magnetic fields.

questions.q: A proton, an electron and an α-particle enter at right angles to a uniform magnetic field with the same velocity. If R$_p$, R$_e$ and R$_\alpha$ are the radii of circular paths of these particles, then
questions.explanation: r = mv/(qB). With the same v and B: R$_\alpha$ = (4m$_p$)v/(2eB) = 2R$_p$, and since m$_p$ ≫ m$_e$, R$_p$ ≫ R$_e$. Hence R$_\alpha$ > R$_p$ > R$_e$.

questions.q: Biot-Savart law indicates that an electron moving with a velocity $\vec V$ produces a magnetic field $\vec B$ around it such that
options: $\vec B$ is inclined to $\vec V$ by 45°
questions.explanation: By the Biot-Savart law, $\vec B \propto \vec V \times \hat r$, so $\vec B$ is always perpendicular to $\vec V$.

questions.q: Two identical circular current loops carrying equal currents are placed with their axes inclined at 45° to each other as shown in the figure. The resultant magnetic field at P is [Figure: two identical circular current loops of radius R carrying current I; point P lies on the axis of each loop at a distance $\sqrt3 R$ from its centre, with the two axes inclined at 45° to each other, one along the x-axis and the other tilted 45° from it]
questions.explanation: Each loop's on-axis field at distance $\sqrt3R$ has magnitude $\dfrac{\mu_0IR^2}{2(R^2+3R^2)^{3/2}}=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{16\sqrt2R}$ directed along its own axis; resolving both fields along the x and y directions (axes inclined at 45°) and adding gives the resultant $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{16\sqrt2 R}[(\sqrt2+1)\hat i+\hat j]$.

questions.q: Two thin long parallel wires separated by a distance 'r' from each other in vacuum carry a current of I ampere in opposite directions. Then, they will
options: Attract each other with a force per unit length of $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r^2}$
Attract each other with a force per unit length of $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}$
Repel each other with a force per unit length of $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}$
Repel each other with a force per unit length of $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r^2}$
questions.explanation: Currents in opposite directions repel each other; the force per unit length between two long parallel wires is $\dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi r}$.

questions.q: A solenoid is 1 m long and 4 cm in diameter. It has five layers of windings of 1000 turns each and carries a current of 7A. The magnetic field at the centre of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: $n=5000$ turns/m. $B=\mu_0 nI=4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5000\times7\approx4.4\times10^{-2}$ T.

questions.q: Two similar galvanometers are converted into an ammeter and a milliammeter. The shunt resistance of ammeter as compared to the shunt resistance of milliammeter will be
questions.explanation: Using $S=\dfrac{I_gG}{I-I_g}$, a wider full-scale range (ammeter) needs a much smaller shunt than a milliammeter, so the ammeter's shunt resistance is less. KEA's initial key had said 'More', but the revised key corrected this to 'Less'.

questions.q: Identify the correct statement
options: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is non-uniform
A current carrying conductor produces an electric field around it.
A straight current carrying conductor has circular magnetic field lines around it.
The direction of magnetic field due to a current element is given by Flemings Left Hand Rule
questions.explanation: A straight current-carrying conductor produces concentric circular magnetic field lines around it (right-hand rule); the field inside an ideal solenoid is fairly uniform, and it is the magnetic (not electric) field that a current produces.

questions.q: Which of the following graphs represents the variation of magnetic field B with perpendicular distance 'r' from an infinitely long, straight conductor carrying current?
options: curve decreasing steadily, steep near origin (graph 3)
questions.explanation: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\propto 1/r$, a hyperbolic curve that falls steadily as r increases, as in graph 3.

questions.q: A moving electron produces
questions.explanation: A moving charge constitutes a current and produces both an electric field (due to its charge) and a magnetic field (due to its motion).

questions.q: A coil having 9 turns carrying a current produces magnetic filed $B_1$ at the centre. Now the coil is rewounded into 3 turns carrying same current. Then the magnetic field at the centre $B_2=$
questions.explanation: Rewinding the same wire into fewer turns increases the radius proportionally ($r\propto N$); since $B\propto N/r\propto N^2$, reducing N from 9 to 3 (a factor of 1/3) gives $B_2=B_1/9$.

questions.q: A particle of specific charge $\dfrac{q}{m}=\pi\,Ckg^{-1}$ is projected the origin towards positive x-axis with the velocity $10\,ms^{-1}$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec B=-2\hat kT$. The velocity $\vec v$ of particle after time $t=\dfrac{1}{12}s$ will be (in $ms^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: The cyclotron period is $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}=\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi\times2}=1\,s$; in $t=\dfrac{1}{12}s=\dfrac{T}{12}$ the velocity turns through $30^\circ$, giving $\vec v=10\cos30^\circ\hat i+10\sin30^\circ\hat j=5(\sqrt3\hat i+\hat j)$.

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius R carrying current I is 64 times the magnetic field at a distance x on its axis from the centre of the coil. Then the value of x is
questions.explanation: $B_{centre}=64B_{axis}\Rightarrow(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}=64R^3=(4R)^3\Rightarrow R^2+x^2=16R^2\Rightarrow x=R\sqrt{15}$.

questions.q: A charged particle is subjected to acceleration in a cyclotron as shown [two D-shaped dees D$_1$, D$_2$ with an oscillator RFO connected across the gap, magnetic field $\vec B$ into the plane, particle spiralling outward]. The charged particle undergoes increase in its speed
options: Inside D$_1$, D$_2$ and the gaps
Only in the gap between D$_1$ and D$_2$
questions.explanation: Inside the dees there is only a magnetic field, which changes direction of velocity but not speed; the particle is accelerated (speed increases) only by the electric field in the gap between the dees.

questions.q: A proton and an alpha-particle moving with the same velocity enter a uniform magnetic field with their velocities perpendicular to the magnetic field. The ratio of radii of their circular paths is

A moving coil galvanometer is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to 5 mA. The galvanometer resistance is 90 Ω and the shunt resistance has a value of 10 Ω. If there are 50 divisions in the galvanometer-turned-ammeter on either sides of zero, its current sensitivity is
questions.explanation: By the shunt condition I$_g$R$_g$=(I−I$_g$)R$_s$: 90I$_g$=(5mA−I$_g$)10, giving I$_g$=0.5 mA for full-scale (50 divisions). Sensitivity = 50/0.5mA = 1×10$^5$ div/A.

questions.q: A positively charged particle of mass m is passed through a velocity selector. It moves horizontally rightward without deviation along the line $y=\dfrac{2mv}{qB}$ with a speed v. The electric field is vertically downwards and the magnetic field is into the plane of the paper. Now, the electric field is switched off at t = 0. The angular momentum of the charged particle about origin O at $t=\dfrac{\pi m}{qB}$ is [figure: axes with the particle's line of motion at height $y_0=2mv/(qB)$ above O, $\vec v$ rightward, $\vec E$ downward, $\vec B$ into the page]
questions.explanation: With E off, the particle moves in a circle of radius r=mv/(qB) under B alone. Direct calculation of L about O at t=πm/(qB) (half a revolution) gives 4m²v²/(qB) = 4m²E²/(qB³), which does not exactly match any option; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question in this version, so option D (the standard-form answer closest to this type of problem) is kept here as the best estimate.

questions.q: A metallic rod of mass per unit length 0.5 kg m$^{-1}$ is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 30$^\circ$ with the horizontal. A magnetic field of strength 0.25 T is acting on it in the vertical direction. When a current 'I' is flowing through it, the rod is not allowed to slide down. The magnitude of current required to keep the rod stationary is
questions.explanation: For equilibrium along the incline, the horizontal magnetic force's component balances gravity: $BI\cos\theta = \lambda g \sin\theta$, giving $I=\lambda g\tan\theta/B=(0.5\times9.8\times\tan30^\circ)/0.25\approx11.32$ A.

questions.q: A circular coil of wire of radius 'r' has 'n' turns and carries a current 'I'. The magnetic induction 'B' at a point on the axis of the coil at a distance $\sqrt{3}$ r from its centre is

A proton moves with a velocity of 5 $\times$ 10$^6$ $\hat{j}$ m s$^{-1}$ through the uniform electric field, $\vec{E}=4\times10^6[2\hat{i}+0.2\hat{j}+0.1\hat{k}]$ Vm$^{-1}$ and the uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}=0.2[\hat{i}+0.2\hat{j}+\hat{k}]$ T. The approximate net force acting on the proton is
questions.note: Computing $\vec v\times\vec B=(1,0,-1)\times10^6$ and adding to $\vec E$ gives $\vec E+\vec v\times\vec B\approx(9,0.8,-0.6)\times10^6$ Vm$^{-1}$, magnitude $\approx9.06\times10^6$, so $F=q|\vec E+\vec v\times\vec B|\approx1.45\times10^{-12}$ N ($\approx14.5\times10^{-13}$ N) - closest to option D, not B; KEA's key credits option B.
questions.explanation: Net force $\vec F=q(\vec E+\vec v\times \vec B)$; KEA's key credits a magnitude of $\approx5\times10^{-13}$ N (see note for the full vector calculation).

questions.q: A solenoid of length 50 cm having 100 turns carries a current of 2.5 A. The magnetic field at one end of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: $n=N/L=100/0.5=200$ turns/m. Field at the centre of a long solenoid $=\mu_0 nI=4\pi\times10^{-7}\times200\times2.5\approx6.28\times10^{-4}$ T; at the end it is half of this, $\approx3.14\times10^{-4}$ T.

questions.q: A strong magnetic field is applied on a stationary electron. Then the electron
options: Moves in the direction of the field
Moves in an opposite direction of the field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is $q\vec v\times\vec B$; since v = 0 for a stationary electron, the force is zero and it remains stationary.

questions.q: Two parallel wires in free space are 10 cm apart and each carries a current of 10A in the same direction. The force exerted by one wire on the other [per unit length] is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{F}{l}=\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1I_2}{2\pi d}=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10\times10}{2\pi\times0.1}=2\times10^{-4}$ N/m; currents in the same direction attract.

questions.q: A toroid with thick windings of N turns has inner and outer radii R$_1$ and R$_2$ respectively. If it carries certain steady current I, the variation of the magnetic field due to the toroid with radial distance is correctly graphed in: (A) B falling from $\mu_0NI/2R_1$ to $\mu_0NI/2R_2$ between R$_1$ and R$_2$. (B) B curving down from $\mu_0NI/2\pi R_1$ towards $\mu_0NI/2\pi R_1$ (hyperbolic fall) between R$_1$ and R$_2$. (C) B rising from 0 to $\mu_0NI/2\pi R_2$ between R$_1$ and R$_2$. (D) B constant at $\mu_0NI/\pi(R_1+R_2)$ between R$_1$ and R$_2$, and zero outside.
questions.explanation: For a toroid with thick windings, treating the effective mean radius $(R_1+R_2)/2$, the field between the radii is approximately constant, $B\approx\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2\pi\cdot\frac{R_1+R_2}{2}}=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{\pi(R_1+R_2)}$, zero outside — matching graph (D).

questions.q: A tightly wound long solenoid has 'n' turns per unit length, a radius 'r' and carries a current I. A particle having charge 'q' and mass 'm' is projected from a point on the axis in a direction perpendicular to the axis. The maximum speed of the particle for which the particle does not strike the solenoid is
questions.explanation: Inside the solenoid $B=\mu_0nI$; the particle moves in a circle of radius $R=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$ and just grazes the solenoid wall when $2R=r$ (the circular path's diameter equals the solenoid radius as it starts at the axis), giving $v_{max}=\dfrac{qBr}{2m}=\dfrac{\mu_0nIqr}{2m}$.

questions.q: The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular coil to its magnetic moment is 'x'. If the current and the radius both are doubled, the new ratio will become
questions.explanation: $B/m=\dfrac{\mu_0 I/2r}{I\pi r^2}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi r^3}=x$; doubling $r$ alone in the denominator (current cancels) makes the new ratio $x/8$.

questions.q: Two long straight parallel wires are a distance 2d apart. They carry steady equal currents flowing out of the plane of the paper. The variation of magnetic field B along the line xx' is given by [xx' is the line joining the two wires; each option is a graph of B vs position along xx', with the two wires marked by dashed vertical lines]
options: graph forming a single smooth hump above the axis between the wires (touching the axis exactly at each wire, with no divergence there) and dipping below the axis outside each wire
graph diverging to $\pm\infty$ at each wire, positive just outside the left wire and negative just outside the right wire, falling from $+\infty$ to $-\infty$ across the gap between the wires

graph diverging to $\pm\infty$ at each wire, negative just outside the left wire and positive just outside the right wire, falling from $+\infty$ (just inside the left wire) through zero at the midpoint to $-\infty$ (just inside the right wire)

graph symmetric about the midpoint: a U-shape between the wires touching zero exactly at the midpoint and rising to $+\infty$ at both wires, with the field diverging to $-\infty$ just outside each wire and decaying to zero far away
questions.explanation: Taking the wires at x=$-d$ and x=$+d$ (both currents out of the page), the field contributions point in opposite senses inside the gap: B(x) = $\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi}\left[\frac{1}{x+d}-\frac{1}{d-x}\right]$ for $-d<x<d$, which is $+\infty$ just inside the left wire, 0 at the midpoint (x=0), and $-\infty$ just inside the right wire. Outside the pair, the two contributions add instead of cancelling: for $x<-d$ the sum is entirely negative (0 to $-\infty$), and for $x>d$ it is entirely positive ($+\infty$ to 0). This asymmetric (odd-symmetric about the midpoint) pattern matches option (C), not the mirror-flipped (B) or the fully symmetric, always-non-negative-looking (A)/(D).

questions.q: In the given figure, the magnetic field at 'O' [a wire carries current I, bent into a $\tfrac34$ circular arc of radius r plus a straight semi-infinite segment ending level with O]
questions.explanation: The $\tfrac34$ circular arc contributes $\tfrac34\left(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2r}\right)=\dfrac{3\mu_0I}{8r}$ and the straight semi-infinite wire contributes $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi r}$; both add at O, giving option (D).

questions.q: The magnetic field at the origin due to a current element $i\,d\vec l$ placed at a point with vector position $\vec r$ (measured from the origin) is
questions.explanation: Since $\vec r$ here points from the origin (field point) to the source, the vector from source to field point is $-\vec r$; the Biot-Savart law $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi}\dfrac{d\vec l\times(-\vec r)}{r^3}$ simplifies to $\dfrac{\mu_0i}{4\pi}\dfrac{\vec r\times d\vec l}{r^3}$.

questions.q: A cyclotron is used to accelerate protons ($^1_1$H), Deuterons ($^2_1$H) and $\alpha$-particles ($^4_2$He). While exiting under similar conditions, the minimum K.E. is gained by
questions.explanation: Exit K.E. in a cyclotron $\propto q^2/m$; taking proton as 1 unit, deuteron gives $\tfrac{1^2}{2}=0.5$ and alpha gives $\tfrac{2^2}{4}=1$, so the deuteron gains the minimum K.E.

questions.q: A long cylindrical wire of radius R carries a uniform current I flowing through it. The variation of magnetic field with distance 'r' from the axis of the wire is shown by
options: graph with a curved rise for r<R, curved fall for r>R, peaking at r=R
graph flat (constant B) for r<R, then falling for r>R
graph with a straight-line rise for r<R and a curved 1/r fall for r>R, peaking at r=R
questions.explanation: Inside the wire $B\propto r$ (linear increase, by Ampere's law for enclosed current), and outside $B\propto 1/r$; the field peaks at $r=R$, matching option (D).

questions.q: In a cyclotron a charged particle
options: speeds up between the dees because of the magnetic field.
slows down within a dee and speeds up between dees
questions.explanation: Between the dees the electric field speeds the particle up, and inside a dee the magnetic force keeps changing its direction (centripetal acceleration), so it is accelerating throughout its motion.

questions.q: The number of turns in a coil of Galvanometer is tripled, then
options: Voltage sensitivity increases 3 times and current sensitivity remains constant
Voltage sensitivity remains constant and current sensitivity increases 3 times
Both voltage and current sensitivity remains constant
Voltage and current sensitivity both decreases by 33%
questions.explanation: Current sensitivity $=\dfrac{NAB}{k}$ increases 3 times with N, while voltage sensitivity $=\dfrac{NAB}{kR}$ also depends on resistance which increases with N (R $\propto$ N), so it stays constant.

questions.q: A circular current loop of magnetic moment M is in an arbitrary orientation in an external uniform magnetic field $\vec B$. The work done to rotate the loop by 30$^\circ$ about an axis perpendicular to its plane is
questions.explanation: The magnetic moment M is along the axis perpendicular to the loop's own plane; rotating the loop about that very axis does not change the angle between M and $\vec B$, so no work is done.

questions.q: A toroid has 500 turns per metre length. If it carries a current of 2A, the magnetic energy density inside the toroid is
questions.explanation: Field inside toroid $B = \mu_0 nI = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\times500\times2 = 1.257\times10^{-3}$ T; energy density $u = B^2/2\mu_0 \approx 0.628$ J/m$^3$.

questions.q: [Figure shows a circular arc carrying current I, with a small 60$^\circ$ gap (dashed) in the circle of radius R, centered at O] The magnetic field at the centre 'O' in the given figure is
questions.explanation: The current-carrying arc spans $360^\circ-60^\circ=300^\circ = \dfrac{5}{6}$ of a full circle, so $B = \dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R} = \dfrac{5}{12}\dfrac{\mu_0I}{R}$.

questions.q: The correct Biot-Savart law in vector form is
questions.explanation: Using the position vector $\vec{r}$ (not the unit vector), the Biot-Savart law is d$\vec{B}$ = ($\mu_0$/4$\pi$) I(d$\vec{l}$ × $\vec{r}$)/r³.

questions.q: An electron is moving in a circle of radius r in a uniform magnetic field B. Suddenly the field is reduced to B/2. The radius of the circular path now becomes
questions.explanation: Since r = mv/(qB) and speed v is unchanged, r ∝ 1/B; halving B doubles the radius to 2r.

questions.q: A charge q is accelerated through a potential difference V. It is then passed normally through a uniform magnetic field, where it moves in a circle of radius r. The potential difference required to move it in a circle of radius 2r is
questions.explanation: r = mv/(qB) with v = $\sqrt{2qV/m}$, so r ∝ $\sqrt{V}$. To double r, V must be increased 4 times, i.e. 4V.

questions.q: A cyclotron's oscillator frequency is 10 MHz and the operating magnetic field is 0.66 T. If the radius of its dees is 60 cm, then the kinetic energy of the proton beam produced by the accelerator is

A proton, a deuteron and an α-particle are projected perpendicular to the direction of a uniform magnetic field with same kinetic energy. The ratio of the radii of the circular paths described by them is
questions.explanation: $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$. For proton ($m,q$): $r\propto1$; deuteron ($2m,q$): $r\propto\sqrt2$; alpha ($4m,2q$): $r\propto \sqrt4/2=1$. Ratio $=1:\sqrt2:1$.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω is connected to a battery of 3V along with a resistance of 2950 Ω in series shows full-scale deflection of 30 divisions. The additional series resistance required to reduce the deflection to 20 divisions is
questions.explanation: Total resistance for full scale (30 div) $=3000\,\Omega$, current $=1$ mA. For 20 divisions, current $=\dfrac{2}{3}$ mA, needing total resistance $=\dfrac{3}{(2/3)\text{mA}}=4500\,\Omega$. Extra resistance $=4500-3000=1500\,\Omega$.

questions.q: The magnetic field at the center of a current carrying loop of radius 0.1 m is $5\sqrt5$ times that at a point along its axis. The distance of this point from the centre of the loop is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{B_{center}}{B_{axis}} = \dfrac{(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}{R^3} = 5\sqrt5 = 5^{3/2}$, so $R^2+x^2 = 5R^2 \Rightarrow x=2R=0.2$ m.

questions.q: A straight wire of length 50 cm carrying a current of 2.5 A is suspended in mid-air by a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T (as shown in figure, with current I flowing horizontally and field B directed into the page). The mass of the wire is (g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: For equilibrium, $BIL = mg \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{0.5\times2.5\times0.5}{10} = 0.0625$ kg $= 62.5$ gm.

questions.q: A proton is projected with a uniform velocity 'v' along the axis of a current carrying solenoid, then
options: the proton will be accelerated along the axis.
the proton path will be circular about the axis.
the proton move along helical path.
the proton will continue to move with velocity 'v' along the axis.
questions.explanation: Inside the solenoid $\vec B$ is along the axis; since $\vec v \parallel \vec B$, the magnetic force $q\vec v \times \vec B = 0$, so the proton moves unaffected with velocity v along the axis.

questions.q: In the cyclotron, as radius of the circular path of the charged particle increases ($\omega$ = angular velocity, v = linear velocity)
questions.explanation: In a cyclotron $\omega = qB/m$ is independent of radius (constant), while $v=\omega r$ increases as r increases.

questions.q: A conducting wire carrying current is arranged as shown. The magnetic field at 'O' [Figure: two straight radial wire segments meet at a point away from O making an angle of 60° between them as seen from O, and are joined by a circular arc; the two straight segments (extended) would pass through O and lie at radii $R_1$ (outer arc) and $R_2$ (inner arc) from O, with current i flowing along one radial segment, around the arc, and back along the other radial segment]
questions.explanation: The straight radial segments produce no field at O; the two arcs (angle $60°=\pi/3$) carry current in opposite sense about O, giving $B=\dfrac{\mu_0 i\theta}{4\pi}\left[\dfrac1{R_1}-\dfrac1{R_2}\right]=\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{12}\left[\dfrac1{R_1}-\dfrac1{R_2}\right]$.

questions.q: A galvanometer coil has a resistance of 50 $\Omega$ and the meter shows full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA. This galvanometer is converted into voltmeter of range 0 - 20 V by connecting
questions.explanation: Series resistance $R=\dfrac{V}{I_g}-G=\dfrac{20}{5\times10^{-3}}-50=4000-50=3950\,\Omega$.

questions.q: A long solenoid with 40 turns per cm carries a current of 1 A. The magnetic energy stored per unit volume is _______ J/m$^3$.

Two concentric coils each of radius equal to $2\pi$ cm are placed at right angles to each other. If 3 A and 4 A are the currents flowing through the two coils respectively. The magnetic induction (in Wb m$^{-2}$) at the centre of the coils will be
questions.explanation: $B_1=\mu_0(3)/(2r)$, $B_2=\mu_0(4)/(2r)$ with $r=0.02\pi$ m; since the coils are perpendicular, $B=\sqrt{B_1^2+B_2^2}=\mu_0(5)/(2r)=5\times10^{-5}$ T.

questions.q: A proton beam enters a magnetic field of $10^{-4}$ Wb m$^{-2}$ normally. If the specific charge of the proton is $10^{11}$ C kg$^{-1}$ and its velocity is $10^9$ ms$^{-1}$, then the radius of the circle described will be
A cyclotron is used to accelerate
options: both positively and negatively charged particles
questions.explanation: A cyclotron can accelerate any charged particle, positive or negative (with the dee-voltage polarity matched to the sign of the charge); it cannot accelerate neutral particles such as neutrons.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω gives a full scale deflection for a current $5\times10^{-4}$ A. The resistance that should be connected in series with the galvanometer to read 3 V is
questions.explanation: Total resistance needed $=V/I=3/(5\times10^{-4})=6000\,\Omega$; series resistance $=6000-50=5950\,\Omega$.

questions.q: Two parallel wires 1 m apart carry currents of 1 A and 3 A respectively in opposite directions. The force per unit length acting between these two wires is
questions.explanation: $F/L=\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times1\times3}{2\pi\times1}=6\times10^{-7}$ N/m; opposite currents repel.

questions.q: A charged particle experiences magnetic force in the presence of magnetic field. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: The particle is moving and magnetic field is parallel to velocity.
The particle is stationary and magnetic field is parallel.
The particle is moving and magnetic field is perpendicular to the velocity.
The particle is stationary and magnetic field is perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Magnetic force F = qv \times B is maximum (non-zero) when the particle moves with velocity perpendicular to B; a stationary charge feels no magnetic force.

questions.q: If a velocity has both perpendicular and parallel components while moving through a magnetic field, what is the path followed by a charged particle?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular component causes circular motion while the parallel component gives uniform motion along the field, combining to give a helical path.

questions.q: A solenoid has length 0.4 cm, radius 1 cm and 400 turns of wire. If a current of 5 A is passed through this solenoid, what is the magnetic field inside the solenoid?
questions.explanation: B = $\mu_0$nI with n = N/l; taking the printed length (0.4 cm) literally gives an unrealistically huge field, so the intended length was likely 0.4 m — this inconsistency is probably why KEA awarded a grace mark. With l = 0.4 m, n = 1000/m and B = 4$\pi$\times10^{-7}\times1000\times5 $\approx$ 6.28\times10^{-3} T (option 1).

questions.q: A gyromagnetic ratio of the electron revolving in a circular orbit of hydrogen atom is 8.8 \times 10^{10} C kg$^{-1}$. What is the mass of the electron? Given charge of the electron = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} C.
questions.explanation: Gyromagnetic ratio = e/(2m), so m = e/(2\times ratio) = 1.6\times10^{-19}/(2\times8.8\times10^{10}) = \dfrac{1}{11}\times10^{-29} kg.

questions.q: What is the value of shunt resistance required to convert a galvanometer of resistance 100 $\Omega$ into an ammeter of range 1A? Given: Full scale deflection of the galvanometer is 5 mA.
A circular coil of radius 10 cm and 100 turns carries a current 1A. What is the magnetic moment of the coil?
A proton and helium nucleus are shot into a magnetic field at right angles to the field with same kinetic energy. Then the ratio of their radii is
questions.explanation: $r=\sqrt{2mKE}/(qB)$. For a proton ($m,\,q=e$) versus a He nucleus ($4m,\,q=2e$) at the same $KE$: $r_p/r_{He}=\dfrac{\sqrt{m}/e}{\sqrt{4m}/2e}=1$.

questions.q: In the diagram, I$_1$, I$_2$ are the strength of the currents in the loop and straight conductors respectively. OA = AB = R. The net magnetic field at the centre O is zero. Then the ratio of the currents in the loop and the straight conductors is [a circular loop of radius R carrying current I$_1$ is centred at O; point A lies on the loop directly below O; a long straight horizontal wire carrying current I$_2$ passes through point B, a further distance R below A]
questions.explanation: Field at O due to the loop $=\dfrac{\mu_0I_1}{2R}$; field at O due to the wire (at distance $2R$) $=\dfrac{\mu_0I_2}{2\pi(2R)}=\dfrac{\mu_0I_2}{4\pi R}$. Equating (opposing directions) gives $I_1/I_2=\dfrac{1}{2\pi}$.

questions.q: Two tangent galvanometers, which are identical except in their number of turns, are connected in parallel. The ratio of their resistances of the coils is 1 : 3. If the deflections in the two tangent galvanometers are 30$^\circ$ and 60$^\circ$ respectively, then the ratio of their number of turns is
questions.explanation: For a tangent galvanometer $I\propto n\tan\theta$, and in parallel the branch currents satisfy $I\propto1/R$. Depending on which coil is taken to have the larger resistance, the turns ratio works out to 1:1 or 9:1, so the question is ambiguous; KEA granted grace marks for it.

questions.q: A charged particle with a velocity 2 $\times$ 10$^3$ ms$^{-1}$ passes undeflected through electric field and magnetic fields in mutually perpendicular directions. The magnetic field is 1.5 T. The magnitude of electric field will be
questions.explanation: For a velocity selector (undeflected path), $qE=qvB$, so $E=vB=2\times10^3\times1.5=3\times10^3\ \text{NC}^{-1}$.

questions.q: A straight current carrying conductor is kept along the axis of a circular loop carrying current. The force exerted by the straight conductor on the loop is _______.
options: perpendicular to the plane of the loop
in the plane of the loop, away from the center
in the plane of the loop, towards the center
questions.explanation: The magnetic field of the straight wire at every point of the loop is tangential to the loop, i.e. parallel to the current element there, so $d\vec F = I\,d\vec l\times\vec B = 0$ everywhere; the net force is zero.

questions.q: Pick out the WRONG statement.
options: The gain in the K.E. of the electron moving at right angles to the magnetic field is zero.
When an electron is shot at right angles to the electric field, it traces a parabolic path.
An electron moving in the direction of the electric field gains K.E.
An electron at rest experiences no force in the magnetic field.
questions.explanation: The electric force on an electron is opposite to $\vec E$ since its charge is negative; if it moves along the direction of $\vec E$, the force opposes its motion and it loses (not gains) K.E., so statement (3) is wrong.

questions.q: Magnetic field at a distance r from an infinitely long straight conductor carrying a steady current varies as
questions.explanation: By Ampere's law, $B=\mu_0I/2\pi r \propto 1/r$.

questions.q: In the loop shown, the magnetic induction at the point 'O' is [figure: current I flows in along a straight line, turns into a quarter-circle arc of radius R$_1$, jumps outward and returns as a quarter-circle arc of radius R$_2$, then continues straight out through O]
questions.explanation: Each quarter-circular arc contributes $\mu_0I/8R$ at O and, from the geometry, the two contributions add, giving $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{8}\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}+\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{8}\cdot\dfrac{R_1+R_2}{R_1R_2}$.

questions.q: An $\alpha$-particle and a proton moving with the same kinetic energy enter a region of uniform magnetic field at right angles to the field. The ratio of the radii of the paths of $\alpha$-particle to that of the proton is
questions.explanation: $r=\sqrt{2mK}/(qB)$; for the alpha particle $m_\alpha=4m_p$ and $q_\alpha=2q_p$, so $r_\alpha/r_p=\sqrt4/2=1$, i.e. 1:1.

questions.q: The torque required to hold a small circular coil of 10 turns, area 1 $mm^2$ and carrying a current of $\left(\dfrac{21}{44}\right)$A in the middle of a long solenoid of $10^3$ turns/m carrying a current of 2.5A, with its axis perpendicular to the axis of the solenoid is ................... [The coil is placed coaxially inside a long solenoid, with the coil's axis perpendicular to the solenoid's axis]
questions.explanation: Field inside solenoid $B=\mu_0nI=4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10^3\times2.5=\pi\times10^{-3}$ T; torque $\tau=NiAB=10\times(21/44)\times10^{-6}\times\pi\times10^{-3}\approx1.5\times10^{-8}$ N-m.

questions.q: A particle of charge $e$ and mass $m$ moves with a velocity $v$ in a magnetic field $B$ applied perpendicular to the motion of the particle. The radius $r$ of its path in the field is .............
questions.explanation: Equating magnetic force to centripetal force, $evB=mv^2/r$, gives $r=mv/(Be)$.

questions.q: A neutron, a proton, an electron and an $\alpha$-particle enter a region of uniform magnetic field with the same velocities. The magnetic field is perpendicular and directed into the plane of the paper. The tracks of the particles are labelled in the figure. The electron follows the track ............ [Figure: all four particles enter moving upward from a common point; track C continues almost straight up (least deflection), tracks A and B curve to the left with A curving more sharply than B, and track D curves to the right]
questions.explanation: With velocity upward and $B$ into the page, the magnetic force $q\vec v\times\vec B$ pushes positive charges (proton, $\alpha$) to the left and the negative electron to the right, while the uncharged neutron goes straight; so the electron follows the track curving right, i.e. D.

questions.q: The deflection in a moving coil galvanometer is reduced to half when it is shunted with a $40\,\Omega$ coil. The resistance of the galvanometer is .....................
questions.explanation: Deflection halving means the shunt carries an equal share of current as the galvanometer, i.e. $\dfrac{S}{G+S}=\dfrac12 \Rightarrow G=S=40\,\Omega$.

questions.q: A current of $\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\right)$A produces a deflection of $60^0$ in a tangent galvanometer. The reduction factor is .................
questions.explanation: For a tangent galvanometer $I=K\tan\theta$, so $K=I/\tan\theta=(2/\sqrt3)/\sqrt3=2/3$ A.

questions.q: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius $R$ due to current $I$ flowing through it is $B$. The magnetic field at a point along the axis at distance $R$ from the centre is .........
questions.explanation: $B_{center}=\mu_0I/2R$; $B_{axis}(x=R)=\dfrac{\mu_0IR^2}{2(R^2+R^2)^{3/2}}=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R\times2\sqrt2}=\dfrac{B}{\sqrt8}$.

questions.q: Two thick wires and two thin wires, all of same material and same length, form a square in three different ways $P$, $Q$ and $R$ as shown in the figure [each shows a square/diamond loop carrying current $I$, with thick and thin wire sides arranged differently]. With correct connections shown, the magnetic field due to the current flow, at the centre of the loop will be zero in case of .................
questions.explanation: The net field at the centre vanishes only when the thick (low-resistance) and thin (high-resistance) sides are arranged symmetrically about the centre, as in $P$ and $R$, so that contributions from opposite sides cancel exactly; the arrangement in $Q$ is asymmetric and leaves a net field.

questions.q: $PQ$ and $RS$ are long parallel conductors separated by certain distance. $M$ is the midpoint between them [$PQ$ carries 2A, $RS$ carries 1A, both upward]. The net magnetic field at $M$ is $B$. Now, the current 2A is switched off. The field at $M$ now becomes .....................
questions.explanation: At $M$, the fields due to the two (oppositely directed, since $M$ lies between them) wires give $B=k(2-1)=k$, where $k=\mu_0/2\pi d$. Switching off the 2A wire leaves only the 1A wire's field at $M$, again of magnitude $k$ (though reversed in direction) — the same magnitude $B$.

questions.q: An electron enters the space between the plates of a charged capacitor as shown. The charge density on the plate is $\sigma$. Electric intensity in the space between the plates is $E$. A uniform magnetic field $B$ also exists in that space perpendicular to the direction of $E$. The electron moves perpendicular to both $\vec E$ and $\vec B$ without any change in direction [crossed-field velocity selector]. The time taken by the electron to travel a distance $l$ in that space is .................
questions.explanation: For the electron to travel undeflected, $qE=qvB\Rightarrow v=E/B$. With $E=\sigma/\epsilon_0$, time $t=l/v=\dfrac{\epsilon_0lB}{\sigma}$.

questions.q: A horizontal metal wire is carrying an electric current from the north to the south. Using a uniform magnetic field, it is to be prevented from falling under gravity. The direction of this magnetic field should be towards the .....................
questions.explanation: For the magnetic force $I\vec L\times\vec B$ on the south-flowing current to point upward, $\vec B$ must point east (right-hand rule).

questions.q: A current $I$ is flowing through the loop. The direction of the current and the shape of the loop are as shown in the figure. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is $\dfrac{\mu_0I}{R}$ times ..................... ($MA=R$, $MB=2R$, $\angle DMA=90^0$) [loop $MABCD$: a quarter arc of radius $R$ from $M$ to $A$, straight segment $A$ to $B$, an arc of radius $2R$ from $B$ back around to $D$, and a straight segment $D$ back to $M$]
options: $\dfrac{7}{16}$, but out of the plane of the paper.
$\dfrac{7}{16}$, but into the plane of the paper.
$\dfrac{5}{16}$, but out of the plane of the paper.
$\dfrac{5}{16}$, but into the plane of the paper.
questions.explanation: Summing the Biot–Savart contributions of the arcs of radii $R$ and $2R$ (the straight segments through $M$ contribute nothing) gives a net field of $\dfrac{7}{16}\dfrac{\mu_0I}{R}$, directed into the plane of the paper (as per KEA key).

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $240\ \Omega$ allows only 4% of the main current after connecting a shunt resistance. The value of the shunt resistance is
questions.explanation: $I_gG=I_sS \Rightarrow 0.04I\times240=0.96I\times S \Rightarrow S=\dfrac{9.6}{0.96}=10\ \Omega$.

questions.q: A coil of 'n' number of turns is wound tightly in the form of a spiral with inner and outer radii 'a' and 'b' respectively. When a current of strength I is passed through the coil, the magnetic field at its centre is
questions.explanation: Treating the spiral as continuous turns $dN=\dfrac{n\,dr}{b-a}$ and integrating $dB=\dfrac{\mu_0 I\,dN}{2r}$ from $a$ to $b$ gives $B=\dfrac{\mu_0 nI}{2(b-a)}\ln\dfrac{b}{a}$.

questions.q: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is independent of
options: magnetic field in which it is lying
questions.explanation: $m=NIA$ depends only on the loop's turns, area and current, not on any external magnetic field it is placed in.

questions.q: A direct current I flows along the length of an infinitely long straight thin walled pipe, then the magnetic field
options: is zero only along the axis of the pipe
is zero at any point inside the pipe
is maximum at the centre and minimum at the edges
is uniform throughout the pipe but not zero
questions.explanation: By Ampere's law, a closed loop of radius $r$ inside the pipe encloses no current (all of it flows on the thin wall), so the magnetic field is zero everywhere inside.
